ordered_diagnoses: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome

facts.raw_span: A 43-year-old woman presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding
Family history was significant for prostate cancer in her father and paternal grandfather
No physical examination findings were explicitly mentioned in the case report
Dilation and curettage was performed
Tumor stained negative for MSH6 protein
MSI testing was negative
Germline mutation R1331X was detected in the MSH6 gene

No physical examination findings were explicitly mentioned in the case report

Germline mutation R1331X was detected in the MSH6 gene

concepts.why: The patient's family history of prostate cancer and the detection of a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene suggest Lynch syndrome.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with endometrial cancer.
The tumor stained negative for MSH6 protein and the patient has a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene, suggesting MSH6-related endometrial cancer.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

concepts.preferred_label: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
concepts.why: The patient's family history of prostate cancer is not directly related to hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome, but it is a possible consideration given the family history of cancer.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with sporadic endometrial cancer.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia.
The patient's family history of prostate cancer and the detection of a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene suggest Lynch syndrome-associated endometrial cancer.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with type II endometrial cancer.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with uterine serous carcinoma.

rationales.F01: Abnormal vaginal bleeding is a common symptom of endometrial cancer.
rationales.F02: Family history of prostate cancer may indicate a hereditary cancer syndrome such as Lynch syndrome.
rationales.F05: Loss of MSH6 protein expression is often seen in sporadic endometrial cancer, but the absence of this finding does not rule out MSH6-related endometrial cancer.
rationales.F06: Negative MSI testing suggests that the tumor may not have a high level of microsatellite instability, which is often seen in Lynch syndrome-associated endometrial cancer.
rationales.F07: The presence of a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene is highly suggestive of Lynch syndrome and MSH6-related endometrial cancer.
